name: Writing Studies
notes: At least six courses including one core course, minimum 22 credits.

FOUR TRACKS: General Writing Studies (take at least one course from each of the other three tracks) plus three specialized tracks - Language/Linguistics/Writing, Digital and Multimodal Communication, and Theory and Practice in Writing and Speaking - each of which requires 3 of the 6 courses from that track. THE GENERAL TRACK IS WHAT IS ENCODED HERE. For a specialized track, take three courses from your track instead of one from each.
WRTG 103, WRTG 104 and all versions of WRTG 105 may NOT be used for the minor.
Courses cannot be taken pass/fail and you must earn at least a 2.0 average in them.
No major and minor may overlap by more than two courses; no two minors may overlap by more than two courses.

PROFESSIONAL WRITING (27X) COURSES: no more than one 27X course counts toward the minor, and all 27X courses are two credits - which is why the minor states a 22-credit floor alongside the six-course count. They all require the primary writing requirement first.
WRTG 267 (Legal Writing and Analysis) is temporarily discontinued and WRTG 290B is not currently offered.

requirementGroups.label: One core course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Core Courses. Analysis of writing at different textual levels (these courses also include practice). Students must select at least one course from the following: WRTG 250/LING 161: Modern English Grammar; WRTG 251/LING 160/ENGL 288: The Playful Sentence; WRTG 252/ENGL 136: Principles and Practices of Copyediting; WRTG 253/BCSC 163: Cognition & Writing; WRTG 265/PHIL 106/ENGL 284: Writing Across the Disciplines: Argument and Evidence; WRTG 282: Research Methods in Writing Studies

requirementGroups.label: Language, linguistics, and writing
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Language, Linguistics, and Writing Track (3 of the 6 courses must be from this track): WRTG 250; WRTG 251; WRTG 253; WRTG 263/ENGL 289/LTST 263: Translation: Interpreting & Adapting; WRTG 290B: Topics: Writing About and With Artificial Intelligence; LING 162/AAAS 162: Modern African-American English

requirementGroups.label: Digital and multimodal communication
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Digital and Multimodal Communication Track (3 of the 6 courses must be from this track): WRTG 247; WRTG 260/DMST 260; WRTG 261/ENGL 288/DMST 250; WRTG 263/ENGL 289/LTST 263; WRTG 290A: Topics: Extended Reality, Communication, and the Metaverse; WRTG 290B (not currently offered); WRTG 370: Creating Digital Identities; BUS 201: Impactful Presentations (valid starting Fall 2026); DMST 200: Digital Portfolio (valid through Spring 2026)

requirementGroups.label: Theory and practice in writing and speaking
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Theory and Practice in Writing and Speaking (3 of the 6 courses must be from this track): BUS 201; WRTG 245/ENGL 285; WRTG 247; WRTG 252/ENGL 136; WRTG 262/BIOL 274W; WRTG 265/PHIL 106/ENGL 284; WRTG 266/GSWS 276 prior to F2023/PHIL 108 beginning F2024; WRTG 267: Legal Writing and Analysis (temporarily discontinued); WRTG 370; WRTG 396/BIOL 396W

requirementGroups.label: Two further writing-studies courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Minor requirements: at least 6 courses including 1 core course, minimum 22 credits.
requirementGroups.note: Students may apply two non-WSAP writing-focused courses (AHST 209, BCSC 207, ENGL 132, ENGL 134, ENGL 135 and others on the page) toward the minor, but no more than one creative-writing course.
